bugs.description: disputes counts dyadic MIDs initiated BY the country, not 'initiated against' it as the code comment (line 84) and the paper text state. Lines 81-82 keep rows with stateb == country and dyad_rolea == 3 (state A is the dyadic target), so the country (state B) is the dyadic initiator.
bugs.evidence: dyadic_mid_4.02.csv is directed (share of rows with a mirror row = 1); codebook DYAD_ROLEA: 1 = initiator, 3 = target; among the 5168 rows the code keeps, dyad_roleb values = 1:5168. Example rows:   disno statea stateb dyad_rolea dyad_roleb sideaa sideab strtyr | 1     2      2    200          1          3      1      0   1902 | 2     2      2    200          1          3      1      0   1902 | 3     2    200      2          3          1      0      1   1902 | 4     2    200      2          3          1      0      1   1902. Information only: recounting with the country as target gives M2 r = 0.1214 (CI 0.0900078;0.152574, p = 5.5e-14) and M1 r = 0.0462; same sign and significance as the paper. Details: outputs/code_review.md, outputs/mid_direction_check.csv.

env_fixes: diffs/README.md: no author file changed. Original CSVs downloaded with ?format=original; working directory set to the file folder.

diffs/README.md: process clock set to 2025-05-06 with faketime, because peacesciencer::create_stateyears(mry = TRUE) ends the frame at Sys.Date() year minus 1; with the real 2026 clock N becomes 17706 and T4/T5 move (T1-T3 unchanged).
diffs/README.md: logr 1.3.8, common 1.1.3, peacesciencer 1.1.0 pinned via remotes::install_version; R 4.5.0 vs authors' 4.3.3; minor tidyverse component drift.
class_reason: All five targets match the paper to its rounding with the authors' unchanged code in a clean library with pinned versions and the clock set to the authors' run date (rebuilt data identical to shipped data: True); the shipped RData gives the same numbers.
confidence_reason: Exact match by script, but it needed an environment judgement (faketime) and the journal's CI digits (T2, T3, T5) could not be read from the journal itself; A/B agreement not yet known.
uncertainties: Without the clock fix (real date 2026-10-09) T4 and T5 do not match: see target notes; class would be B (T4 rel diff about +2.7%, T5 about +3.9%). I judged the clock setting an environment fix because no code changes and the authors' LOG.pdf shows the run date 2025-05-06.

Journal CI digits: Wiley HTML (web_fetch) drops the CI brackets; pdfdirect and /pdf/ failed; curl got HTTP 403. T2/T3 agree with the author preprint (peterbils.com 2024-06) and with an exa.ai index excerpt of the journal text. T5 ([.03963]) could not be confirmed from any open copy I read; the preprint has an older M1 result (0.05132).
R_b (outlier exclusion) changes the significance conclusion of M2: r = 0.0111, p = 0.50 after dropping 123 rows. R_a and R_c keep a positive significant estimate.

pub_def == 1 filter (replication.R line 24) keeps 3811 country-years with exactly one public defensive alliance; the paper's sample wording ('member of a public defensive alliance') would give 8645 rows (pub_def max 14). Whether '== 1' is intended cannot be determined; recorded as a discrepancy, not a bug.

M1 text says 'defensive secret alliances' and a yearly MID sum; code uses all secret alliances (secret, not secret_def) at country-year level. Information only: with yearly secret_def r = 0.0555; a system-year version (209 years) gives r = -0.0953. Reported number matches the code; intent undeterminable; not counted as a bug.
secret_alliances counts alliance memberships (an alliance with k members counts k times), not distinct alliances (155 years differ). Information only: distinct count gives M2 r = 0.1686.
Paper says MIDs 5.0; code uses dyadic MID 4.02 (ends 2014), so 2015-2024 country-years have disputes = 0 by construction. Documented in the code; not a bug.
README names AJPS_rep.RData and codebook.pdf; the Dataverse has AJPS_analysis_data.RData and no project codebook. Did not block reproduction.
peacesciencer 1.1.0 pulled stevemisc 1.9.0 (current CRAN); the authors' stevemisc version is not recorded. No effect seen (rebuilt data identical to shipped).

The sandbox was recycled mid-run (R removed and reinstalled by another agent's setup_env.sh); the first as-is run (runA) happened before the recycle, the wrapper runs after. Both real-clock runs gave the same numbers.
